faqs.question: What does the Mantoux test (5TU) measure?
faqs.answer: The Mantoux test measures your immune system's response to the tuberculosis bacteria.

faqs.question: Why is the Mantoux test (5TU) done?
faqs.answer: • To screen and diagnose tuberculosis • To assess the risk of developing TB • To evaluate treatment effectiveness • To diagnose other conditions that affect tuberculosis or related infections

faqs.question: When is the Mantoux test (5TU) recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: The Mantoux test is recommended when there is a suspicion of tuberculosis infection. It is done for individuals with known exposure to TB, symptoms suggestive of TB, or conditions that weaken the immune system. The test is suitable for people of all ages, including infants, children, and adults.

faqs.question: What if the results of the Mantoux test (5TU) are abnormal?
faqs.answer: A positive result indicates exposure to tuberculosis, but it does not confirm an active infection or disease. Abnormal results could suggest other conditions affecting the immune system.

faqs.question: What to expect during the Mantoux test (5TU)?
faqs.answer: During the test, a small amount of TB protein will be injected just under your skin. The reaction to the test is read after 72 hours by a healthcare professional.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before the Mantoux test (5TU)?
faqs.answer: • Inform your doctor about any medications you are currently taking to ensure proper interpretation of the test results. Also, tell them if you have any specific requirements. • Follow any specific instructions given by your healthcare provider.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with the Mantoux test (5TU)?
faqs.answer: Other tests that may be ordered alongside the Mantoux test include sputum analysis, blood tests for TB antibodies, and TB culture tests.

faqs.question: What is the Mantoux test Tuberculin test (5TU) also known as?
faqs.answer: Tuberculin skin test or Purified protein derivative (PPD) skin test

faqs.question: What is tuberculosis (TB)?
faqs.answer: Tuberculosis (TB) is a contagious bacterial infection caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis. It primarily affects the lungs but can also affect other parts of the body. TB spreads through the air when an infected person coughs or sneezes, and it can be treated with antibiotics.
